releases.overview: Follow-up fix to the placement bulk-edit released an hour earlier.
highlights: Fixes a problem fetching placements, introduced by the v1.5.18 placement work.

FLAG — the version number looks wrong: this shipped as v1.15.19 barely an hour after v1.5.18, so it was almost certainly meant to be v1.5.19. Worth confirming with whoever tagged it, since a mis-numbered tag makes rollbacks and version comparisons unreliable.

releases.overview: Bulk editing for campaign placements, with a review-and-confirm step.
highlights: New placement bulk-edit flow with a review dialog before changes are applied.
Several bugs caught in review and fixed before release: blank slots were being written as 0%, no-op reviews fired redundant updates, and untouched slots weren't visually distinct from edited ones.
Also fixed in-memory filters being wiped on unrelated URL changes, and a query firing before its date/campaign inputs were ready.

releases.overview: Metrics filter added to the placement reporting APIs.
highlights: Completes the backend side of the placement filtering work.
Deployed about 75 minutes before the frontend release that uses it — correct order this time.

releases.overview: Helix dashboard: long Project Manager summaries no longer get clipped.
highlights: The Project Manager card was pinned to a fixed height, so a long meeting summary was hidden behind an inner scrollbar and a long headline overflowed the card. It now sizes to its content.
Also carries early Placement Modifier groundwork that isn't user-facing yet.

releases.overview: Placement API filter options updated.
highlights: Small backend update to the filter options on the placement APIs.
Supports the placement UI work landing the same day.

releases.overview: Image Studio performance table: negative sales figures now read correctly.
highlights: Overall Sales rendered a bare signed number while neighbouring columns used a coloured arrow, so a negative sales change looked neutral. It now shows as currency with a direction arrow.
Also clears misleading "-0%" cells that showed a red down-arrow for a value that rounds to zero.

releases.overview: Content Studio jobs performance dashboard updated.
highlights: Changes to the Jobs performance dashboard in Content Studio.
This is the release whose formatting treatment gets reused by the Image Studio table the following day.

releases.overview: EC2/scheduler pair catches up to the search-term reporting migration.
highlights: No new code — brings the EC2 backend and scheduler to the same commit already live on ECS.
Note the version numbering: the EC2 pipeline reuses numbers that don't line up with the ECS "-backend" series, which makes the two easy to confuse.

releases.overview: Search-term reports now read from a new aggregated data source.
highlights: Search-term reporting was migrated to a new v2 aggregate metrics table — a data-source change, so figures are worth spot-checking against the old view.
Fixed a bug where search-term period rows were being silently discarded from the metrics view.
Highest-risk item this week for reporting accuracy: worth a deliberate comparison pass.

releases.overview: Placement reporting gains column configuration and filters.
highlights: Placement endpoints now support column configuration and filtering, and their response shape changed.
Sponsored Brands campaigns gained a bid-optimisation toggle.

releases.overview: Content Studio: changes to the view-versions section.
highlights: Adjustments to the version-comparison view in Content Studio.
Third small Content Studio deploy within three hours — the day saw four frontend releases.

releases.overview: Content Studio: changes to external ASIN handling.
highlights: Touches how external ASINs are handled in Content Studio.
Commit messages are terse, so scope beyond "external ASIN" isn't documented.

releases.overview: Single ticket merged with no descriptive commit message (XNEETI-2928).
highlights: One pull request, titled only with its ticket number — the change isn't described in the commit history.
Check the ticket to know what to verify.

releases.overview: Content Studio tweaks — small, loosely described changes.
highlights: Assorted Content Studio adjustments; the underlying commits are labelled only as "changes" and "few tweaks", so the precise scope isn't recoverable from history.
Worth a quick smoke test of Content Studio rather than a targeted regression pass.

releases.overview: Content Studio keyword-source fix reaches ECS, plus a scheduler change.
highlights: View Keywords shows the true keyword source (database/manual) rather than labelling everything AI-generated.
Scheduler no longer advances 15 tier-1 tables automatically.

releases.overview: New Competitor Search Terms view on the Growth Competition Scorecard.
highlights: A fourth sub-tab shows which search terms competitor ASINs rank for, filterable by cohort, ASIN, and resolution.
The competitor list in the previous sub-tab now links straight into it, pre-filtered to that ASIN.
Paired with backend support deployed the same afternoon — this one went out in the right order.

releases.overview: Second EC2/scheduler catch-up of the day, following the afternoon's ECS releases.
highlights: No new code — brings the EC2 backend and scheduler up to the same commit deployed to ECS earlier.
Two EC2 deploys in one day is unusual for this pipeline.

releases.overview: Content Studio regeneration now reports a dedicated ML-owned status.
highlights: Regeneration writes a separate status field owned by the ML pipeline, replacing a timeout-based guess about whether work finished.
Also carries the competitor-terms reporting work.

releases.overview: Competitor search terms added to the Competition Scorecard, plus an Image Studio status fix.
highlights: Competitor search terms now appear as a section of the Competition Scorecard and are included in both exported workbooks.
Fixed an Image Studio job status-change bug.
Also bundled: shared dependency bump and the heap-snapshot shipper sidecar.

releases.overview: Internal only: multi-threshold heap-snapshot capture merged in.
highlights: Continues the memory-diagnostics work — no user-visible change.
Purely operational tooling for diagnosing memory pressure.

releases.overview: Small fix to Image Studio notification logging.
highlights: Corrected notification logs for Image Studio jobs.
Narrow, single-purpose deploy 30 minutes after the previous one.

releases.overview: Backend groundwork for placement reporting and competitor search-term harvesting.
highlights: New endpoints for fetching placement information and reports — the backend behind the placement work that reaches the UI later this week.
Created the competitor search-term harvest tables that feed the new Competition Scorecard view.
Sponsored Brands campaigns gained a bid-optimisation option.

releases.overview: Content Studio UI fixes, including keyword highlighting.
highlights: Fixed keyword highlighting in Content Studio.
Assorted Content Studio UI bug fixes and an added improvement section.

releases.overview: Catches the EC2 backend + scheduler pair up to code already running on ECS.
highlights: No new code of its own — this pipeline deploys the EC2 backend and the scheduler together, which the ECS pipeline never touches.
First EC2/scheduler deploy since Aug 11, so it picks up roughly a week of backend changes in one jump.

releases.overview: Memory diagnostics for the backend, plus a Content Studio keyword-source display fix.
highlights: The backend can now capture a heap snapshot when memory crosses configurable thresholds, and ship those snapshots to S3 for diagnosis — follow-up to the earlier memory-crash safety net.
Content Studio's View Keywords now shows the real keyword source instead of defaulting everything to "AI".
Scheduler change: 15 tier-1 tables no longer auto-advance.

releases.overview: Notification threshold fix, plus several small UI corrections.
highlights: Fixed notification threshold handling.
Disabled sections in the UI behave better, and a request payload bug was corrected.
Mixed bag of small frontend fixes rather than one themed change.

releases.overview: Image Studio approval fixes plus groundwork for Content Studio content regeneration.
highlights: Fixed Image Studio slot approval and the client-approval carry-over between job states.
Content Studio regeneration now pre-clones the target version before handing off to ML, and has a timeout with an explicit failed/completed outcome instead of hanging.
The scheduler no longer takes part in new-org onboarding data sync.

releases.overview: Growth reporting frontend gains Sponsored Brands / Sponsored Display breakdowns.
highlights: Frontend half of the SB/SD growth-reporting work — reporting screens can now show the per-ad-type split rather than blended figures.
Bounded release: this was the only pull request in the commit range.

releases.overview: No new code — a redeploy of the same commit already live as v1.5.5.
highlights: No commits landed on master between v1.5.5 and this deploy, so nothing functional changed.
Most likely a pipeline re-run or environment/config change rather than a code release.

releases.overview: Backend endpoints powering the Campaign Master report, deployed just after its frontend half.
highlights: Adds the three reporting endpoints the new Campaign Master sub-tabs call.
A planned campaign (profile, date) database index was deliberately dropped from this release along with a reporting window change.
Arrived ~3 minutes after the frontend that depends on it — worth watching the deploy order on paired changes.

releases.overview: New Campaign Master report shipped — every campaign broken down by ad product, with the attribution behind each one.
highlights: Three sub-tabs (Sponsored Products / Brands / Display), each with its own sortable columns, status filter, and name-or-ID search.
Each ad product gets its own sales-attribution panel, because the shapes genuinely differ — SP shows four look-back windows, SD separates view-through from click-attributed.
Real export bug fixed: the Export button previously ignored the active search and status filter, so "Queried result" silently downloaded the same workbook as "Full result".
Deployed roughly 3 minutes BEFORE the backend endpoints it calls (v1.1.34-backend) — a brief window where these tabs could have failed in production.

releases.overview: Display fix: the Reduce Spend tab now shows readable action names instead of raw values.
highlights: The "Last Change" column showed values like "bid_decreased" — it now reads "bid decreased".
Display-only change, scoped to the Reduce Spend tab components.

releases.overview: Small fix: sidebar navigation and hover states in collapsed sections.
highlights: Sub-items inside collapsed left-nav sections now behave consistently as clickable links, with clearer hover and keyboard focus.
Tightly scoped change — only the sidebar hover work came along with it.

releases.overview: Backend half of the Sponsored Brands reporting rollout, paired with the same day's v1.5.2 frontend deploy.
highlights: New Sponsored Brands/Sponsored Display data across five reporting screens, each split by ad type instead of blended.
Fixed data-accuracy bugs in Term Cohort Summary counts and the Defense/Competition Excel export.
Went out about 100 seconds AFTER its frontend half — the intended order was backend first.

releases.overview: New Sponsored Brands report tab added to the internal Growth reporting dashboard.
highlights: A Sponsored Brands report tab now sits alongside the existing Sponsored Products report, with its own relevant columns.
Blended SP+SB figures on several summary/defense reports can now be expanded to see the split behind them.
Content for this entry predates the commit range that was re-verified, so the detail here is carried over from the original hand-kept log.

releases.overview: Small fix: campaign reports now show readable bid-strategy names instead of raw codes.
highlights: Campaign reports now translate bid-strategy codes into human-readable names.
Any strategy value not recognized by the translation still displays unchanged — nothing gets hidden or broken for edge cases.

releases.overview: Notification subscriptions: added buy-box and content-change filtering, fixed a partial-update bug.
highlights: Notification subscriptions can now be filtered by buy-box status and content-change fields, with the older field name still supported for existing subscriptions.
Fixed a bug where changing just one setting on a subscription was wiping its other existing filters.
Subscription values are now validated and normalized consistently, including uppercase inputs.

releases.overview: Internal reliability: backend now restarts itself gracefully before it would otherwise crash from memory pressure.
highlights: Backend memory usage had been climbing sharply during the morning traffic burst and crashing both running copies at once within ~15 minutes.

The backend now watches its own memory and, before it would crash, restarts itself in a controlled way (draining active requests first) — the crash becomes an unnoticeable routine restart instead of a hard outage.
This is a safety net, not the root-cause fix — engineers can now also opt in to a memory snapshot for diagnosing the underlying cause as a follow-up.

releases.overview: Real incident fixed: users were getting locked out of login for up to 2 hours after a role change.
highlights: Confirmed real incident: after an admin changed someone's role, a caching bug could remember they had no roles for up to 2 hours — so they'd see "not authorized" even though their new role was valid.
Cause: an empty role lookup was being cached and trusted for 2 hours. An empty/invalid cached result is never trusted now, so a role change takes effect on the very next login.
Self-healing: any already-affected cache entries fix themselves on the next login attempt — no manual cleanup needed.
Also bundled: lowered 5 oversized Image Studio background workers from up to 100x concurrency down to 5x, as preventive protection against memory-crash risk.

releases.overview: Same code as v1.1.28-backend, now also rolled out to the EC2 backend+scheduler pair.
highlights: No new code — this catches the EC2/scheduler pair up to the same version deployed to ECS a few minutes earlier.
Brings the Content Studio uploads fix, the View Keywords API, and regenerate-endpoint groundwork to the scheduler and EC2 backend as well.

releases.overview: New: View Keywords modal API for Content Studio, plus regenerate-endpoint groundwork.
highlights: New backend API powers a View Keywords modal for Content Studio job versions — one endpoint covers all 5 tabs with per-keyword status and search-volume stats.
Backend groundwork only: the content-regenerate endpoint now accepts tags on added keywords and a new highlight section, ready for when the frontend sends them — no confirmed frontend usage yet.

releases.overview: Real bug fixed: Content Studio uploads were being falsely marked "Upload Failed" even when they succeeded.
highlights: Root cause: the system checked an upload against the wrong Amazon API (one that holds aggregated product attributes, not the seller's actual listing text) — so the check was always empty, and jobs got auto-flagged "Upload Failed" at timeout regardless of whether the upload worked.
Confirmed against 4 real, incorrectly-stuck jobs across 3 different client orgs before this fix.
Now verifies against the correct API, and tolerates formatting differences (smart quotes, spacing) so real matches aren't missed.

Also fixes: a listing that hasn't propagated yet on Amazon's side is now treated as pending/retry instead of a false mismatch, and duplicate completion emails for the same upload can no longer happen.

releases.overview: Advertising search now matches partial terms and ignores case.
highlights: Search across campaigns, ad groups, ads, keywords, search terms, and portfolios now matches partial terms and is case-insensitive — it was previously an exact, case-sensitive match that missed obvious results.
Result counts now stay consistent with the filtered results actually shown.

releases.overview: Image Studio UI enhancements now fully live — frontend catches up with the previous day's backend deploy.
highlights: Undo slot approval and undo slot finalisation are now available in the UI, matching what shipped on the backend the day before.
Job-incomplete navigation guard and the "Send Feedback / Mark Approved" prompts are confirmed live in production.
Creative Studio / Image Studio now defaults to the Jobs tab on landing, and Global Admins can view in-progress job slots read-only.
Bundled Image Studio Replication polish: correct image-version ordering, more accurate loading states, and a fixed hero-image upload validation bug.

releases.overview: New: Undo Approval and Undo Finalisation for Image Studio job slots.
highlights: A Global Admin can now undo an approval on an Image Studio slot while it's still awaiting review — it reverts to Feedback or back to Finalised.
A Designer can now undo a finalisation while the job is still on their desk — it reverts to Draft so it can be edited and re-finalised.
Both actions are immediate (no confirmation dialog) and are logged to the job's activity timeline.

releases.overview: Fixed billing lock-in dates showing one day early for clients outside India.
highlights: Confirmed on a real client account: plan lock-in dates displayed one calendar day earlier than what was on file for anyone in a timezone west of UTC (e.g. US clients).
Root cause was display-only — the underlying stored date was always correct, so this drove no billing or invoicing impact, only an incorrect date shown.
Fixed across all 4 places lock-in dates are shown: the sign-agreement page, Settings → Billing, the downloadable plan PDF, and the ops agreement preview.
Retroactively corrects the display for all 33 orgs that had already signed — no data migration needed.

releases.overview: Same code as v1.1.24-backend, now also rolled out to the EC2 backend+scheduler pair.
highlights: No new code — catches the EC2/scheduler pair up to the version deployed to ECS about an hour earlier.
Brings the new Search Term Cohorting backend support to the scheduler and EC2 backend as well.

releases.overview: New: Search Term Cohorting added to the Growth module.
highlights: New backend support for grouping search terms into cohorts — start a cohort build, monitor its run status, and browse paginated cohort/term lists with filters.
Bug fixes bundled in: corrected cohort-member status handling for ASIN filtering, and made default-profile selection consistent for orgs with more than one seller profile.
Honest signal: the incremental cohort-sync endpoint (versus a full rebuild) isn't implemented yet, and now clearly says so instead of silently doing the wrong thing.

releases.overview: Same code as v1.1.23-backend, now also rolled out to the EC2 backend+scheduler pair.
highlights: No new code — catches the EC2/scheduler pair up two increments: the Opportunity Center cooldown/display fixes and the Content Studio regulated-category upload fix.

releases.overview: Fixed Content Studio uploads failing for regulated categories (Beauty/Personal-Care).
highlights: Uploading approved content to Seller Central returned a generic error for regulated categories — confirmed on real listings — because the request asked Amazon to revalidate the entire listing, and those categories fail on unrelated compliance fields.
Now only the actually-changed content is validated, fixing the regulated-category failures with no change for categories that already worked.
Upload failures now return a clear, specific reason, and the job stays in "Client Approved" status so it can be retried instead of getting stuck.

releases.overview: Content Studio: new Product Highlight support, plus several workflow improvements.
highlights: New Product Highlight support across Content Studio — generation, editing, feedback, keyword spotlighting, and review.
New active filter and sort chips in keyword management for easier filtering.
Jobs now default to newest-first sorting with role-specific statuses and review actions.
Bug fixes: keyword and calendar views now refresh reliably after changes, and job archiving requires confirmation and can't be duplicated.

releases.overview: Opportunity Center: cooldown periods now respected correctly, plus a display fix for bid/spend actions.
highlights: Sponsored Brands and keyword opportunity matching now correctly respects each entity's configured cooldown period, replacing an outdated fixed 7-day rule — fewer wrong recommendations for things still in cooldown.
Fixed the "Last Change Action" column showing the wrong action; empty values now show consistently blank instead of inconsistent data.

releases.overview: Opportunity Center: CSV export for negative-keyword data, plus min/max metric ranges.
highlights: New CSV export for negative-keyword data, with a progress indicator and error notifications if it fails.
Optimization and spend-reduction tables now show a min/max range across the selected lookback period, not just a single number.
Bid and spend actions now use the correct current row values instead of potentially stale ones.

releases.overview: No new code — catches the EC2 backend+scheduler pair up to the version already live on ECS.
highlights: First EC2/scheduler deploy since v1.1.15 — the scheduler picks up six versions of backend changes in one jump, most notably the New Relic agent removal and a large dead-code cleanup.
The ECS pipeline only ever deploys the backend container, never the scheduler — this EC2 pipeline deploys both together as a pair.

releases.overview: Content Studio now waits 7 days (not 48 hours) before marking an Amazon upload as failed.
highlights: Amazon's listing updates can take longer than 48 hours to reflect — that grace window is now 7 days, giving slower propagation room to catch up before a false "failed" is shown.
Expected side effect, not a regression: in-flight "Uploading to Amazon" jobs will now visibly sit in that status roughly 3.5x longer than before.
Self-healing rollout: jobs already uploaded just before this deploy resolve themselves within 48 hours, no manual action needed.

releases.overview: Fixed duplicate org invites caused by email casing (e.g. John@X.com vs john@x.com).
highlights: The Invite Users dialog now treats an email the same regardless of capitalization — previously, typing an existing member's email in different casing bypassed the "already exists" check and sent a duplicate invite.
Known follow-up flagged but not fixed here: the Sign Up page still accepts mixed-case emails.

releases.overview: Fixed a bug in Optimize Bids and Wasteful Spend Detection that was skipping some keywords.
highlights: These features were silently excluding keywords flagged as "disabled" when deciding what to check — now all eligible keywords are considered.
Also bundled: a large internal dead-code removal in the scheduler (zero behavior change) and a couple of internal monitoring additions — only the keyword-eligibility fix is user-facing.

releases.overview: Internal-only: New Relic monitoring removed from the backend, a deliberate tradeoff.
highlights: New Relic APM has been fully removed from the backend and scheduler — the team is relying on CloudWatch and structured JSON logs instead.
Deliberate tradeoff: this gives up transaction traces and per-endpoint performance stats in exchange for lower overhead.
Fixed two bugs found in passing: every request was silently double-logging, and a leftover scheduler hook was calling into an agent that was never initialised.
No user-visible change — purely internal.

releases.overview: Internal-only: fixed broken production logging on the backend.
highlights: Since July 29, every backend error log had been arriving fragmented across ~10 CloudWatch entries with garbled formatting — logs are now clean, single-entry, and searchable.
Also fixed a bug causing every request failure to be logged twice.
No user-visible change — purely an internal observability fix.

releases.overview: Content Studio hotfix: bad ASIN jobs blocked, clearer status labels.
highlights: Content Studio can no longer create or progress a job with no sections selected — users now get a clear error instead of a broken job.
Internally the team now sees "PDP update pending" instead of the confusing "Upload Failed" label — clients still see "Job Completed", unchanged.

releases.overview: Backend fix: @xneeti.com users can now be granted the Xneeti Analyst role.
highlights: Fixed an RBAC bug where inviting or assigning an @xneeti.com user the Xneeti Analyst role failed.
Also presumed included (recently merged, exact boundary unconfirmed): Image Studio Replication backend support and Budget Dayparting campaign-management changes.

releases.overview: Image Studio Replication opened up to all eligible jobs.
highlights: Replication is no longer restricted to a small allow-list of test accounts — now available org-wide for all eligible jobs.
Minor polish to the image-version comparison view: correct ordering and auto-selecting the best available version.

releases.overview: Image Studio Replication shipped to production.
highlights: New: clone an approved creative job onto other product listings instead of rebuilding it from scratch.
Post-launch stability fixes for Replication, plus campaign search and filtering improvements in Advertising.
